### 3.5 Home Blood Pressure Monitoring

All patients in whom a treatment decision has been made under Table 1 should
perform home blood pressure monitoring using a validated upper-arm device.
Patients should take two readings one minute apart in the morning before
medications and two readings one minute apart in the evening, on at least three
and preferably seven consecutive days, and transmit their readings to the care
team weekly through the patient portal, secure messaging, or telephone. The
care team reviews the weekly average systolic and diastolic readings. A home
average of 135/85 mmHg or higher is considered equivalent to an office reading
of 140/90 mmHg. The responsible clinician should be notified when the weekly
home average is 135/85 mmHg or higher, or exceeds a lower threshold set by the
clinician for patients with diabetes or chronic kidney disease; this is a
routine notification unless readings indicate a hypertensive crisis. Any single
reading above 180/120 mmHg should be repeated after five minutes; if it remains
above 180/120 mmHg the patient should contact the clinic the same day.

### 3.6 Follow-up Contact and Outreach

If a week passes without readings, a reminder should be sent to the patient.
After three reminder attempts on different days without readings, the care team
should contact the patient directly to identify barriers to monitoring. For
patients starting or changing medication, the seven-day home average should be
reviewed two to four weeks after the change, in addition to the laboratory
follow-up in Table 2. Patients managed with lifestyle modification alone should
have their home readings reviewed at the follow-up visit scheduled under Table
1.
